Plenty of vids on YouTube that explain mtb suspension. I recommend the ones by a suspension expert. To answer your questions: 1) you dampen the compression to keep the fork from blowing through its travel when it's being compressed.  Air pressure is how much force it takes to hold you up allowing for the recommended sag. Same as a car spring--too weak and the car will scrape the ground and bounce and too stiff and the car will be tall and ride like a wheelbarrow. 2) you have a lower level shock, which the only adjustments are air pressure and rebound damping most likely. 3) if you're bottoming out with the right sag then yes you need to reduce the air chamber with spacers to get a sharper ramp up. Too many volume spacers and the fork will be too stiff and feel like crap though.

You can add all the air you want, but if the compression circuit isn't damped well you'll still blow through travel. You won't bottom out the fork, but on braking the fork will dive easily and then get really stiff as it gets deeper into the travel. A good fork has controlled diving and has good mid travel support so that it doesn't feel like it gets super stiff all of a sudden.  It's not bad to ride with some compression on, but it can make the fork harsh if you put on too much damping.
